messages:
nina: Heads-up: noticed a recurring delta between raw ingest events and the billing ledger for a subset of long-running chat sessions. looks like attribution keys are flipping during tokenization. :frowning:
sam: ugh. do you have an example trace? short one please so we can reproduce.
nina: pasted one below (sanitized):\n```
ingest_event: { session_id: s-123, fingerprint: fA, tokens: [...], attribution_key: tenant:acct:42 }
tokenizer_out: { session_id: s-123, fingerprint: fA, tokens: [...], attribution_key: tenant:acct:42#v2 }
billing_event: { session_id: s-123, fingerprint: fA, billing_key: tenant:acct:42 }
```\nbilling route didn't match because tokenizer appended a version tag.
jordan: sounds like we have non-canonical keys between services. we've seen similar with the prefix-migration. is this only when tokenizer runs async/parallel?
nina: yeah, appears for async tokenization where the tokenizer service appends heuristics (`#v*`) to reduce collisions. ingest doesn't know about that.
tara: quick question — is there a provenance_id in the ingest envelope we can use as stable join key?
evan: in theory `provenance_id` exists for chunked requests but it's optional and not always set for older clients.
sam: options: 1) enforce canonicalization at ingest (strip version tags) 2) have tokenizer set canonical_provenance on output 3) join on fingerprint+session but that feels brittle. tradeoffs?
jordan: (1) adds low-latency work to ingest hot path — risk for perf. (2) requires tokenizer to be trusted to write canonical field upstream — simpler semantics. (3) fallback but will miss some corner cases.
ops-bot: deploy-note: ingest hot-path change would affect 12 services and needs a canary. :warning:
tara: for audits we need an immutable mapping anyway. even if we canonicalize, we should emit a mapping event: `canonical_map: { original_key -> canonical_key }` so audits can replay.
nina: agree. proposal: tokenizer sets `canonical_attribution` and emits a sidecar mapping event; ingest accepts and persists canonical if present. If not present, route to a best-effort postprocess queue and flag for replay. keeps ingest cheap but gives correctness via sidecar.
evan: cost: extra storage + sidecar fanout. benefit: no extra synchronous CPU on ingest. I'm +1 for prototype.
sam: timeline? who picks this up? I can do a small spike to prove mapping event format and cost estimate.
jordan: i'll own the postprocess consumer (best-effort queue) and reconciliation hook for ledger. will stub the metric/reporting.
tara: I'll draft a quick audit playbook for how to run replays when mapping events are late/missing.
nina: thanks — spike + audit playbook sounds perfect. Sam, can you have a spike PR by end of week? even just a test harness and perf numbers.
sam: yes. will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder: please add a canary plan and rollout steps to the PR description if changing ingest behavior.
